name: performance.memory (legacy heap size)
plain: Reads JavaScript heap sizes in Chrome.
meaning: Exposes usedJSHeapSize, totalJSHeapSize and jsHeapSizeLimit, which cluster by device RAM and OS (about 4 GB on 64-bit desktop, 2 GB on mobile). Values are quantized.

fields.name: usedJSHeapSize
fields.precision: bucketed to about 10 KB or quantized

limits.headline: Can see how much memory the page uses, in Chrome and Edge
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page asks
can: Get used, total and limit sizes for the page's memory
Guess your device memory, around 4 GB on desktop and 2 GB on phones
Find memory leaks in its own page
cannot: Get exact values, since they are rounded
limits.differs: Only Chrome and Edge. Firefox and Safari do not support it.

story.what_it_is: An older Chrome feature that reports the size of JavaScript memory, rounded to blur the exact number.
story.for_you: You never see it. It lets a site learn roughly how much memory your tab uses, and a rounded value hints at how much memory your device has. Newer tools have mostly replaced it.
story.for_makers: Developers used it to catch leaks, but it is not precise and not standard. Some fraud and tracking tools read it as a clue to your device class. Chrome blurs the numbers to limit this.

use_cases.example: A developer logs memory use in a test to check that an app does not leak over time.
A browser game watches heap growth to know when to free textures before the tab crashes.
A bot detector sees a heap size that is typical of a headless browser.
A tracker adds the rounded heap limit to a device ID, since it varies by device memory.
A web office app warns you to save when memory use gets high.
A monitoring script records heap size at each page view to find slow releases.
A video call site checks memory on old laptops to decide on lighter effects.

history.change: Values quantized and bucketed to limit fingerprinting
